KEY MESSAGE 1...Pleasant weather for the Labor Day 
Holiday with low humidity and mild temperatures. Dangerous rip
currents continue at east-facing beaches through most of the
day. The dry and pleasant conditions continue through 
Wednesday.

4am Update: Went ahead and issued a Rip Current Statement for
east-facing beaches as well as the islands. Numerous off and
near-shore buoys are still reporting elevated wave periods of
8-10 seconds, which is favorable for the formation of rip
currents and locally hazardous swimming conditions. 

A tranquil Labor Day Holiday is on tap as high pressure builds over 
the Northeast. Aloft, these changes are driven by a broad 500 mb 
ridge sprawling from the mid south into the Northeast. Looking at a 
cool start to the morning after tonight's radiational cooling.  The 
vast majority of locations will wake up to lows this morning in the 
lower to mid 50s with isolated 40s in favored valley locations. 
After a cool start, there's a lot to look forward to with regards to 
today's sensible weather. Temperature-wise it's a seasonably mild 
day with highs warming into the mid and upper 70s. To further 
solidify today as a peak weather day humidity levels will certainly 
be fall-like with dew points in the 40s and low 50s. Only caveat 
will be a somewhat gusty NW wind. A modest low-level jet of 25-30kts 
combined with a well-mixed boundary layer will yield gusts up to 20 
mph. On Tuesday, the deeper mid-level trough continues to shift 
further eastward as a mid-level ridge continues to build in from the 
west. 925mb temperatures warm to +17-18C yielding high temperatures 
in the upper 70s with locations potentially hitting the 80 degree 
mark in the valleys. High pressure in place will support mainly dry 
conditions. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Unsettled weather returns mid to late week but the 
threat for flooding and severe weather appear low at this time. 

By Wednesday, the mid-level ridge begins to break down and the 
pattern becomes more more zonal by Thursday. Guidance continues
to show a series of shortwaves and low pressure systems passing
N of the region with their associated frontal boundaries 
bringing chances for precipitation during the second half of 
the week. Any boundaries that pass through the region will be 
accompanied by a plume of above normal moisture, rising to 
160-190% of normal by early Thursday yielding PWATS of 1.5" 
approaching 2.0". The positioning of an upper jet should supply 
ascent for periods of showers. There is spread across guidance 
in the finer details of the timing of the waves which will 
influence timing of the showers. A shortwave pushes through 
sometime Wednesday evening/night triggering the first round of 
showers which should taper off through the morning Thursday (at 
latest). The next wave moves through late Thursday/Thursday 
Night bringing another round of showers. With the timing of the 
waves still variable across guidance this leaves some 
uncertainty in thunderstorm/downpour potential. There will be 
plenty of moisture to support downpours; however, the timing of 
the wave would need be early enough to tap into the marginal 
instability build through the day for convection. For now, we 
are not seeing a strong signal for severe or flash flooding, 
more likely periods of showers with light accumulations outside 
of any isolated storms/downpours. An 850mb 35- 45kt LLJ shifts 
across southern New England into Thursday. There does raise a 
flag for potentially gustier winds; however, this will come down
to how well we can mix down from 850mb or even 925mb. If things
align, ensembles show potential for gusts in the 20-35 mph 
range on Thursday across the land and coastal waters. Still 
plenty of details to work out in the pattern before we come into
better agreement about the gusts, but something to watch for 
now. 

Temperatures Wednesday/Thursday lean near to slightly above normal 
with temperatures in the mid to upper 70s. A cold front pushes 
through early Friday bringing a cooler airmass this will support 
highs in the upper 60s low 70s.
